source_issues.title: Model, dataset and scale assertions
source_issues.detail: Data-source capacities/mixes, exact Llama3 percentages, universal Wikipedia use,38% duplicates, GPT4 fertility1.3 and industry-standard-since2024 claims are source assertions not verified online. Output quality cannot be causally attributed overwhelmingly to data without controlling architecture/training. The three cited architectures are not identical in every material respect; quantitative source text retained.

source_issues.title: Chinchilla conditions and same-loss statement
source_issues.detail: N and D scale approximately with compute under particular fitted assumptions; this is not a guarantee that10x parameters needs10x tokens for same loss at fixed compute.175B/300B undertrained3-4x lacks an explicit comparator. Compute-optimal versus inference-optimal depends on total deployment workload; overtraining here is not synonymous with overfitting. No model trained or scaling law re-estimated.

source_issues.title: Quality, language and PII scope
source_issues.detail: Confidence<.8 and high perplexity do not universally imply unclean or spam text; language/domain mismatch affects scores. RefinedWeb-specific method attribution not independently verified. Regex/NER cannot promise complete PII removal. Source document code implements neither actual language detector nor PII remover nor perplexity LM; exercises are not completed implementations.

source_issues.title: Destructive cleaner and HTML semantics
source_issues.detail: Regex tag stripping keeps script contents, merges adjacent tag-separated words and does not decode entities. ASCII filter deletes Chinese/accented letters and tabs rather than preserving visible Unicode. URL regex is broad; full multilingual cleaning target is not fulfilled. Fixture output ABalert(1) cafC confirms these limitations.

source_issues.title: Heuristic filter validation
source_issues.detail: 50-word and cap/special ratios are configurable heuristics, not detectors certified for SEO/spam or quality. Acronyms/code/non-English may be rejected. Default empty input rejected, but min_words0 causes division by zero. No actual web corpus was filtered in this review.

source_issues.title: Short documents and exact-duplicate gaps
source_issues.detail: Default5-word shingles of shorter documents are empty; MinHash becomes all infinities and verification skips empty sets, so two identical short documents survive. Long identical fixture removes one. Case/whitespace normalization and word shingling are not bytewise equality. Hash collisions and threshold equality convention remain distinct; prose exceeds versus code >= preserved.

source_issues.title: LSH probability, parameters and worst case
source_issues.detail: LSH candidate selection is approximate; more bands raise candidate recall at fixed hash budget, but exact Jaccard verification affects final false positives. No worst-case near-linear guarantee: one shared bucket still generates all pairs. Nondivisible signature length drops tail values; bands>hash count yields empty bands and arbitrary collisions. MinHash independence/permutation assumptions not proved for the prefix-SHA family.

source_issues.title: Greedy duplicate removal and retention
source_issues.detail: Iterating a set of pairs with skipped removed endpoints is a greedy policy, not connected-component dedup or a guarantee all retained pairs are below threshold. Near-duplicate similarity is not transitive; which representative remains depends on traversal and input ordering. No retention policy or deterministic cross-runtime promise supplied.

source_issues.title: Sequence packing and actual mask
source_issues.detail: Source code flattens documents with EOS and emits only1D padding validity, not block-diagonal or causal pairwise attention masks. It loses document IDs/boundaries needed for independent-document attention, has no loss-label masking, and splits purely by token offset. Diagram lengths sum2048 without EOS budget. Last chunk retains padding, so eliminates-padding-waste is not absolute.

source_issues.title: Streaming, batching and reproducibility
source_issues.detail: tokenize_corpus materializes every token; packing, masks, signatures and shuffled indices also live in lists. Yielding batches alone is not end-to-end bounded-memory streaming. DataLoader seed external/global, no worker sharding or asynchronous throughput guarantee. seq_length0, batch_size0 and mask-shape mismatch fail in fixtures. No GPU/TB benchmark.

source_issues.title: Statistics and units
source_issues.detail: Source compression ratio is Unicode-character-count/token-count, not encoded bytes or stored compression; denominator includes EOS. Utilization hardcodes token!=0: a legitimate ID0 is ignored and nonzero pad_id counted as real. Reproduced .5 instead of mask-based.625, and1 instead of.25 for pad7. Empty token list or zero vocabulary divides by zero.3-4/1.5/8+ and90% are heuristics, not guaranteed diagnoses.

source_issues.title: External comparison and throughput
source_issues.detail: Document says Project Gutenberg then external snippet loads WikiText, so same corpus is not established. It downloads model/dataset, truncates per example at2048 and uses possible map cache. Timing excludes initial loads and exact preprocessing/tokenization differ;4 processes need not equal4 hardware cores,10-50x not measured. Source code was not run; no datasets/transformers/fastText imports/install/downloads.

source_issues.title: Exercise perplexity direction
source_issues.detail: Body removes high perplexity but exercise says bottom20%; ascending perplexity versus quality ranking is ambiguous. Translation preserves ranking-lowest wording without choosing a corrective direction. Character-set heuristic cannot identify English robustly, and exact-hash comparison needs normalization choices. No external corpus or new LM training.
